title: A Mom's Desperate Prayer Gets Answered
paragraphs: So, there's this guy Elkanah from Ramathaim, from the Zuph family line up in the Ephraim hills. (He was tied to the Zuphs from Ephraim through his dad Jeroham, his grandpa Elihu, and his great-grandpa Tohu.) This dude had two wives, which is kinda wild. First wife was Hannah, second was Peninnah. The thing is, Peninnah had a bunch of kids, but Hannah had zero.

Every year, Elkanah would take his fam to Shiloh to worship and give a sacrifice to God. Eli and his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were the priests of God there. During the big meal, he'd give food to Peninnah and all her kids, but he always gave a super-sized portion to Hannah. It was because he loved her a ton and felt bad that she couldn't have kids. But Peninnah was super mean about it. She'd always be throwing shade and making Hannah feel awful that she wasn't a mom. This happened all the time, year after year. Every time they went to church, Hannah knew she was gonna get bullied. It got so bad she would just cry and couldn't even eat.
Her husband Elkanah was like, 'Hannah, what's wrong? Why are you crying and not eating? Why are you so down? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?'

So Hannah finally ate something. Then she got it together, snuck off, and went into the sanctuary. The priest Eli was there, just chilling in his usual spot. Hannah was totally heartbroken. She prayed to God and just bawled her eyes out. Then she made a promise:
'God, if you see how much I'm hurting, and if you'll finally help me out and give me a son, I'll give him right back to you—completely, for his whole life, set apart to live for you.'

So while she was praying before God, Eli the priest was watching her. Hannah was just praying in her head, so her lips were moving but no sound was coming out. Eli totally misread the situation and thought she was drunk. He went up to her and was like, 'You're drunk! How long are you gonna be like this? Sober up!'

Hannah was like, 'Oh no, sir, you've got it all wrong! I'm just a woman with a broken heart. I haven't had a single drop of wine or beer. I'm just pouring out my heart to God. Please don't think I'm a bad person. I'm just so miserable and in so much pain that I've been here for a while.'
Eli then said, 'Go in peace. And may the God of Israel give you what you've asked for.'
'Thank you, and please pray for me!' she said, and then she left. After that, she ate a good meal and looked super happy.
They got up super early the next day, worshiped God, and then went back home to Ramah. Elkanah slept with his wife Hannah, and God started working on her request.
And what do you know, before the year was over, Hannah got pregnant and had a son. She named him Samuel, and she was like, 'I asked God for him.'

When Elkanah and his family went on their yearly trip to Shiloh to worship God, offer sacrifices, and keep his vow, Hannah didn't go. She told her husband, 'After the baby is done breastfeeding, I'll bring him to God myself, and he'll stay there for good.'
Elkanah said to his wife, 'Do what you think is best. Stay home until he's weaned. And let God finish what he started!'

So that's what she did. She stayed home and nursed her son until he was weaned. Then she took him to Shiloh, and she brought a huge sacrifice with her—a bull, flour, and wine. The kid was so young to be sent away!

First, they sacrificed the bull, and then they brought the boy to Eli. Hannah said, 'Excuse me, sir. You're not gonna believe this, but I'm the same woman who was standing right here, praying to God. I prayed for this child, and God gave me what I asked for. And now I'm giving him back to God. He's dedicated to God for his whole life.'
And right then and there, they worshiped God.

title: Hannah's Epic Prayer & The Priest's Sons Who Messed Up BIG TIME
paragraphs: Hannah prayed this:
I'm so full of good news from God, I could burst! I feel like I'm floating. I can finally laugh in the face of my haters. I'm literally dancing because I'm saved.

Seriously, no one is as holy as God. He's the ultimate rock, our God. So don't go acting all high and mighty—no bragging, ever! God sees everything. He knows the real score. The gear of the so-called 'strong' gets totally wrecked, while the weak get a major power-up. The rich kids who had it all are now begging for scraps, while the hungry are getting second helpings. The woman who couldn't have kids now has a full house, while the mom with tons of kids is left with nothing.

God is the one who decides life and death; he can send you to the grave or bring you back up. God can make you poor or make you rich; he can bring you low or lift you high. He helps the poor get back on their feet; he gives burned-out people fresh hope, giving them back their dignity and respect—a spot in the limelight! Because the very foundations of the earth belong to God; his whole operation is built on a solid base. He looks out for his loyal friends, every step of the way, but lets the wicked trip and fall in the dark. You can't get by in this life just by being strong! God's enemies will be blasted out of the sky, crashed in a heap and burned. God will make things right all over the world, he'll give his king a power-up, and put his chosen one on top of everyone.
Then Elkanah went home to Ramah. But the boy, Samuel, stayed behind and served God with Eli the priest.

Eli's sons were a total disaster. They had zero respect for God and couldn't care less about the proper way priests should act. Normally, when someone made a sacrifice, the priest's assistant was supposed to come over while the meat was cooking and stick a three-pronged fork in the pot. Whatever the fork brought up, the priest got to keep. But Eli's sons had their own messed-up system for all the Israelites who came to Shiloh to offer sacrifices to God. Before the fat was even burned as God's portion, the priest's assistant would barge in and say, "Give me some of that meat for the priest to roast. He doesn't want it boiled; he wants it rare." If the person argued back, "Hey, let the fat be burned for God first! Then you can take whatever you want," the assistant would be like, "Nope, I want it now. And if you don't give it to me, I'll just take it." It was a huge sin these guys were committing right in front of God, totally disrespecting the holy offerings.

Meanwhile, there was Samuel, just a kid, serving God in his little priest outfit. And every single year, his mom would make him a new little robe and bring it when she and her husband came for the yearly sacrifice. Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, "May God give you more kids to take the place of this one you gave to God." Then they'd go home.
And God was super good to Hannah. She ended up having three more sons and two daughters! And the boy Samuel grew up right there in the sanctuary with God.

By this time, Eli was ancient. He kept hearing all these reports about how his sons were ripping people off and sleeping with the women who volunteered at the sanctuary. Eli confronted them: "What is this I hear? Why are you doing this stuff? I'm hearing non-stop stories about your corrupt and evil behavior. Oh, my sons, this is so not okay! These are terrible rumors spreading all over the place among God's people! If you sin against another person, God can help. But if you sin against God himself, who's gonna be there to back you up?"

But they were too far gone, completely disobedient, and wouldn't listen to a word their father said. So God, who was totally done with them, decided they had to die. But the boy Samuel was thriving, growing up, blessed by God and liked by everyone.

A man of God came to Eli and said: "This is a message from God: I clearly revealed myself to your ancestors when they were slaves in Egypt. Out of all the tribes of Israel, I picked your family to be my priests: to lead at the Altar, burn incense, and wear the special priest robes in my presence. I put your family in charge of all the offerings from Israel. So why are you treating these sacred offerings, which I commanded for my worship, like they're just loot? Why do you honor your sons more than me, letting them get fat on the best parts of the offerings, while ignoring me? Because of this—this is the word of God, the God of Israel—I once promised that your family would be my priests forever, but now—listen up, this is God's word!—no way can that continue.
I honor those who honor me; but I'll bring down those who look down on me.

"So listen up: the time is coming when I'm going to wipe out your entire family, present and future. No one in your family will live to be old. You'll see all the good things I'm doing in Israel, but you'll just watch and cry, because no one in your family will be around to enjoy it. I'll leave one person to serve at my Altar, but his life will be hard, full of sadness. Everyone else in your family will die young. And the proof will be what happens to your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: they will both die on the same day. Then I'll raise up a faithful priest for myself. He'll do what I want, be who I want him to be. I'll make his position solid, and he'll freely do his work in the service of my anointed one. Any survivors from your family will have to come to him, begging for money, saying, 'Please, can I have some priest-work, just for a little food?'"

title: God's Late-Night Call to Samuel Was WILD
paragraphs: So, the kid Samuel was working for God under Eli. Back then, it was super rare to get a direct message from God or see anything crazy like that.

One night, Eli was totally crashed out. His eyesight was so bad he could barely see anything. It was way before sunrise, but the lamp in the sanctuary was still on. Samuel was sleeping in the Temple of God, right where the Ark of the Covenant was.
Then God called out, “Samuel, Samuel!”
Samuel shot up and said, “Yeah? I’m here.” He ran to Eli and was like, “You called me? What’s up?”
Eli was like, “I didn’t call you. Go back to bed.” So he did.
God called him again, “Samuel, Samuel!”
Samuel got up again and went to Eli, “For real, you called. I’m here.”
Eli said again, “Son, I didn’t call you. Go back to bed.” (This was all before Samuel really knew God for himself, like, before he’d gotten a personal message from God or anything.)
God called out, “Samuel!” for the third time. And for the third time, Samuel got up and went to Eli, “Okay, I definitely heard you call me. I’m here.”

That’s when it finally clicked for Eli that God was the one calling the boy. So he told Samuel, “Go lie down. If you hear the voice again, say, ‘Speak, God. I’m your servant, and I’m listening.’” So Samuel went back to bed.
Then God showed up, stood right there like before, and called out, “Samuel! Samuel!”
Samuel answered, “Speak. I’m your servant, and I’m ready to listen.”

God said to Samuel, “Yo, listen up. I’m about to do something in Israel that’s gonna shake everyone. The time has come for me to drop the hammer on Eli’s family, just like I warned him. Every single word. I’m letting him know that time’s up. I’m bringing judgment on his family for good. He knew his sons were messing up big time, disrespecting my name and my house, and he didn’t do a thing to stop them. So this is the sentence for Eli’s family: Their sin is so bad that no sacrifice or offering will ever be able to cancel it out.”
Samuel stayed in bed till morning. Then he got up early and did his usual chores, opening the doors of the sanctuary. But he was terrified to tell Eli about the vision.
But then Eli called for him, “Samuel, my son!”
Samuel came running, “Yeah? What can I do for you?”
“What did he say? Tell me everything. Don’t you dare leave out or soften a single word, or God will judge you. I want it all, word for word, exactly what he told you.”
So Samuel told him everything, word for word. He didn’t hold anything back.
Eli just said, “He is God. Let him do what he thinks is best.”

Samuel grew up, and God was with him. His track record as a prophet was flawless, for real. Everyone in Israel, from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, knew that Samuel was the real deal—a legit prophet of God. God kept showing up at Shiloh, revealing himself to Samuel through his word.

title: Israel's Epic Fail & The Stolen Ark
paragraphs: Basically, whatever Samuel said went viral all through Israel.

Israel went to war against the Philistines. The Israelites set up their camp at Ebenezer, and the Philistines were at Aphek. The Philistines came out to fight, the battle got intense, and Israel got totally wrecked—like, four thousand of their soldiers were left dead on the field. When the troops got back to camp, the elders of Israel were like, “Yo, why did God let us get beaten so badly by the Philistines today? Let's go to Shiloh and grab the Ark of God's Covenant. It'll roll with us and save us from our enemies.”

So the army sent guys to Shiloh to get it. They brought back the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD of Heaven's Armies, the God who is enthroned between the cherubim. Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, came along with the Ark.

When the Ark of the LORD’s Covenant entered the camp, all the Israelites let out a massive cheer. The shout was so loud it literally shook the ground. The Philistines heard the noise and were like, “What is all that shouting in the Hebrew camp about?”

Then they found out that the Ark of the LORD had arrived in the Hebrew camp. The Philistines totally panicked. “Their gods have come to their camp! This is bad, nothing like this has ever happened before. We're toast! Who can save us from these super-powerful gods? These are the same gods who hit the Egyptians with all those plagues in the wilderness. Get ready, Philistines! Be brave! We're about to be slaves to the Hebrews, just like they were to us. Show 'em what you're made of! Fight for your lives!”

And wow, did they fight. It was a total beatdown. They thrashed Israel so hard that the Israelite soldiers just ran for it, leaving behind a crazy thirty thousand dead soldiers. And if that wasn't bad enough, the Ark of God was captured, and Eli's two sons—Hophni and Phinehas—were killed.

Right away, a guy from the tribe of Benjamin sprinted from the battle lines all the way back to Shiloh. His clothes were torn and he had dirt all over his face. He ran into town, and Eli was sitting on his stool by the road, just watching and waiting, because he was quietly having a panic attack about the Ark of God. When the man ran into town and broke the bad news, the whole town started crying and freaking out. Eli heard the loud wailing and asked, “What’s all this chaos?” The messenger rushed over to tell him. Eli was ninety-eight years old by then, and totally blind. The man told Eli, “I just came from the battle. I barely got away with my life.”
“So what happened, my son?” Eli asked.
The messenger answered, “Israel ran from the Philistines. It was a huge disaster, with massive losses. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the Ark of God has been captured.”

As soon as he mentioned the “Ark of God,” Eli fell backward off his stool right there by the gate. He was an old man and pretty heavy, so when he fell, he broke his neck and died. He had led Israel for forty years.

His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’s wife, was pregnant and about to pop. When she heard that the Ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and her husband were both dead, she collapsed and went into hard labor. As she was dying, the midwife helping her said, “Don’t worry, you had a son!” But she didn't even react, like she didn't hear.

With the Ark of God gone, her father-in-law dead, and her husband dead, she named the boy Ichabod, which means “Glory’s-Gone.” She said, “The glory has been exiled from Israel, because the Ark of God was taken.”

title: God's Ark vs. Fake Idol Goes WILD
paragraphs: So, after the Philistines jacked the Chest of God, they hauled it from Ebenezer to Ashdod. They rolled it right into their god Dagon's temple and stuck it right next to the Dagon statue.

The next morning, the people of Ashdod woke up and were totally shook. Dagon had face-planted right in front of the Chest of God. So they picked him up and put him back. But get this—the *very next morning*, same thing. Dagon was down again, totally bowing to the Chest. This time, though, his head and arms were snapped off and scattered at the doorway. Only his torso was left in one piece. (That's why, to this day, Dagon's priests and anyone visiting his temple in Ashdod make sure not to step on that part of the floor).

Then God went hard on the people of Ashdod. He wrecked them, giving them all these painful tumors. It happened all over town and in the suburbs, too. Then, He unleashed a plague of rats. They came off the ships and just swarmed the whole city. It was wild. Everyone was terrified.

When the Ashdod leaders saw the chaos, they were like, 'Okay, the Israelite God's chest has *got* to go. We can't deal with this, and apparently, neither can our god Dagon.' So they got all the Philistine bosses together and asked, 'What are we gonna do to get rid of this thing?'
The bosses decided: 'Send it to Gath.' So, off the Chest of God went to Gath.
But as soon as it got there, God started messing with Gath, too. Total panic! He hit them with tumors, and they started popping up on everyone in the city, from the kids to the grandparents.

So they passed the Chest of God along to Ekron. But when it showed up, the people of Ekron freaked out, yelling, 'You brought the Chest of the God of Israel here to kill us all!' They called another meeting with the Philistine leaders and begged them, 'Get this Chest of the God of Israel out of here! Send it back where it came from. We're all about to die!' Seriously, everyone was scared to death when the Chest arrived, because God was already coming down hard on the city. The people who didn't die from whatever was happening got hit with tumors. The whole city was just filled with cries of pain.

title: The Ark's Wild Ride Home
paragraphs: After God's Chest had been in Philistine territory for seven months, the Philistine leaders called up their religious experts, the priests and the fortune-tellers, for a meeting. "How do we get rid of this Chest of God?" they asked. "Get it out of here without making things even worse. Tell us what to do!"

They said, "If you're sending the Chest of the God of Israel back, you can't just send it empty. You have to send a gift to make things right. Then you'll be healed, and once you're good again, God will let up on you. Why wouldn't he?"
"Okay, so what kind of gift would be enough?"

"Five gold tumors and five gold rats," they said, "one for each of the Philistine leaders. Since all of you—leaders and people—got hit with the same plague, make little models of the tumors and rats that are wrecking the country and give them as a gift to honor the God of Israel. Maybe then he'll go easy on you, your gods, and your country. Why be stubborn like the Egyptians and Pharaoh? God kept hammering them until they let the people go. Only then did he stop.

"So here's the plan: Get a brand-new cart and two mama cows that have never been worked before. Hitch the cows to the cart and put their calves back in the barn. Put God's Chest on the cart. Then, put the gold models of the tumors and rats you're offering as a gift in a bag and set it next to the Chest. Then just send it off. But watch it closely. If it goes straight back home toward Beth Shemesh, then we'll know this whole disaster was a punishment from God. But if not, we'll know God had nothing to do with it—it was just a freak accident."

So that's what they did. They hitched two cows to the cart, locked their calves in the barn, and put God's Chest and the bag of gold rats and tumors on the cart. The cows went straight for home, right down the road to Beth Shemesh, without turning left or right, mooing the whole way. The Philistine leaders followed them all the way to the edge of Beth Shemesh.

The people of Beth Shemesh were out in the valley harvesting wheat. They looked up, saw the Chest, and were totally stoked. They ran to meet it. The cart came into the field of a guy named Joshua from Beth Shemesh and stopped right next to a giant rock. The workers broke the cart apart, chopped up the wood, and sacrificed the cows as a burnt offering to God. The Levites took the Chest of God and the bag with the gold gifts and placed them on the big rock. By offering sacrifices, everyone in Beth Shemesh had a huge worship session that day.
When the five Philistine leaders saw everything they needed to see, they went back to Ekron that same day.

The five gold tumors were the apology gift from the Philistines for the cities of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron. The five gold rats were for all the Philistine towns, big and small, that the five leaders ruled. That huge rock where they put God's Chest is still there in Joshua of Beth Shemesh's field, a landmark to this day.

But then God struck down some of the men from Beth Shemesh because they got curious and disrespectfully peeked inside God's Chest. Seventy of them died. The whole town was in mourning, completely rocked by the harsh blow from God. They started asking, "Who can even stand before God, this holy God? And who can we get to take this Chest off our hands?"
They sent messengers to Kiriath Jearim with a message: "The Philistines sent back the Chest of God. Come down and get it."

title: God's Thunder Is No Joke
paragraphs: And they did. The guys from Kiriath Jearim came and got the Ark of God and brought it to Abinadab's house up on the hill. They made his son, Eleazar, the guy in charge of it.
The Ark stayed in Kiriath Jearim for a super long time—like, 20 years. And during that time, there was this massive, almost scared, movement of people all over Israel turning back to God.

Then Samuel laid it all out for Israel: “If you’re actually serious about coming back to God, you need to clean house. Get rid of all the foreign gods and those fertility goddess statues. Ground yourselves in God, worship Him and only Him, and He’ll save you from the Philistines who keep messing with you.”
And they actually did it. They tossed out all the fake gods, the statues of Baal and Ashtoreth, and gave their full attention and service to God alone.
Next, Samuel said, “Everyone gather at Mizpah, and I’ll pray for you.”
So everyone showed up at Mizpah. They did this cleansing thing where they drew water from the wells and poured it out before God. They fasted all day and prayed, “We have sinned against God.”
That's how Samuel got the Israelites ready for a holy war there at Mizpah.

When the Philistines heard the Israelites were all meeting up at Mizpah, their leaders decided to go on the attack. The Israelites got the news and were totally terrified—the Philistines were on the move again!
They begged Samuel, “Pray like crazy! Don't stop! Pray to God, our God, that he’ll save us from getting wrecked by the Philistines.”
Samuel took a young lamb and offered the whole thing as a burnt offering to God. He prayed hard for Israel, and God answered.

While Samuel was in the middle of the sacrifice, the Philistines got close enough to start a fight. But right then, God let out a massive thunderclap that exploded right over the Philistines. They totally panicked in the confusion and scattered. The Israelites charged out of Mizpah and chased them down, taking them out left and right, all the way past Beth Car. Samuel set up a big rock between Mizpah and Shen and named it Ebenezer, which means 'Rock of Help,' saying, “This is where God helped us.”

The Philistines learned their lesson and stayed away—no more crossing the border. God was tough on them for Samuel's entire life. All the cities the Philistines had taken from Israel, from Ekron to Gath, were given back. Israel also freed the nearby towns from Philistine control. And for a while, there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

Samuel was a solid leader for Israel his whole life. Every year, he’d do a tour from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, leading Israel in each place. But he always came back to his home in Ramah to lead from there. That's also where he built an altar to God.

title: We Want a King! But Is It a Good Idea?
paragraphs: So, when Samuel got really old, he made his sons judges over Israel. His first son was Joel, and the second was Abijah, and they were in charge down in Beersheba. But his sons were nothing like him at all. They were all about making money, taking bribes, and totally messing with the justice system.

So, all the elders of Israel had enough. They got together and went to Samuel in Ramah to talk. They were like, "Look, you're old, and your sons are not following your example at all. So, do us a solid: give us a king to lead us, just like every other nation."
When Samuel heard them say, "Give us a king to rule us!" he was totally crushed. He thought it was a terrible idea and went straight to God to pray about it.

God told Samuel, "Go ahead, listen to them. It's not you they're rejecting; they're rejecting me as their king. They've been doing this since the day I brought them out of Egypt, always leaving me for other gods. Now they're doing the same thing to you. So, let them have their way. But you have to warn them. Tell them exactly what they're getting into and how a king will rule over them."

So Samuel went back and gave God's warning to the people who were demanding a king. He said, "Okay, so here's the deal with the king you want. He'll draft your sons to be his soldiers—for his chariots and cavalry, and to run with his chariots. He'll force some to work on his farms, plowing and harvesting, and make others build his weapons and chariots. He'll take your daughters and make them work as perfumers, cooks, and bakers. He'll take your best fields, vineyards, and olive groves and just give them to his buddies. He'll tax your grain and your grapes to pay for all his officials. He'll take your best workers and your best animals for his own projects. He'll take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will basically become his slaves. When that day comes, you'll cry out for relief from the king you chose, but don't expect God to answer you then."

But the people wouldn't listen to Samuel. "No!" they insisted. "We want a king over us! Then we'll be like all the other nations, with a king to lead us and to go out before us and fight our battles."
Samuel heard everything they said and went back and told God.
God said to Samuel, "Listen to them and give them a king."
Then Samuel told the men of Israel, "Alright, everyone go back to your own town."

title: Lost Donkeys Lead to a Wild Destiny
paragraphs: So, in the tribe of Benjamin, there was this guy named Kish. He was from a pretty solid family line—son of Abiel, grandson of Zeror, great-grandson of Becorath, great-great-grandson of Aphiah—a Benjaminite. A real stand-up guy. He had a son, Saul, who was legit the most handsome dude around. No joke, he was a whole head taller than everyone else.

One day, some of Kish’s donkeys just up and vanished. Kish told his son, “Saul, take one of the servants and go find those donkeys.” So Saul and a servant bounced. They searched the hill country of Ephraim and around Shalisha, but no luck. Then they hit up Shaalim—still nothing. Then Jabin, and again, nada.
When they got to the Zuph area, Saul was over it. He said to the servant, “Alright, let’s just head back. My dad’s probably stopped worrying about the donkeys and is now stressing about us.”
But the servant was like, “Hold up, there’s a holy man in this town. He’s a big deal, and whatever he says, happens. Maybe he can tell us where to go.”
Saul replied, “But what can we even give him? We’re out of food, and we have nothing to bring the holy man as a gift. You got anything?”

The servant said, “Actually, I’ve got this silver coin. I’ll give it to him, and he’ll tell us what to do!” (Fun fact: back then in Israel, if you wanted to ask God something, you’d say, “Let’s go see the Seer,” because the one we call a “Prophet” now, they used to call a “Seer.”)
“Good idea,” Saul said, “let’s go.” So they went to the town where the holy man lived.
As they were walking up the hill to the town, they ran into some girls coming out to get water. They asked them, “Hey, is the Seer around here?”

They answered, “He sure is—he’s just up ahead. You better hurry. He’s in town today for a special sacrifice. If you go into town right now, you’ll catch him before he goes up to the shrine to eat. No one eats until he gets there to bless the sacrifice. After that, everyone can eat. So get moving, you’ll definitely find him!”
So they kept going and entered the city. And boom, there he was—Samuel!—walking right toward them on his way to the shrine.

Just the day before, God had given Samuel a heads-up: “Tomorrow around this time, I’m sending you a guy from the land of Benjamin. You’re going to anoint him as the leader of my people, Israel. He’s the one who will save them from the Philistines. I’ve seen how much they’re struggling, and I’ve heard their cries for help.”
The second Samuel saw Saul, God was like, “That’s him. That’s the guy I told you about. He’s going to be the one to lead my people.”
Saul went up to Samuel in the street and asked, “Excuse me, can you tell me where the Seer’s house is?”

“I am the Seer,” Samuel said. “Come with me to the shrine and eat with me. In the morning, I’ll tell you everything you want to know and send you on your way. And don’t worry about those donkeys you’ve been looking for for three days—they’ve been found. Right now, the future of all Israel is in your hands.”
Saul was like, “Whoa, what? I’m just a Benjaminite, from the smallest tribe in Israel, and my family is like, the least important one in the whole tribe. Why are you saying all this to me?”

But Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining hall and gave them the best seats at the head of the table, with about thirty other guests. Then Samuel told the chef, “Bring out that special cut of meat, the one I told you to set aside.”
The chef brought it out and set it right in front of Saul, saying, “This was saved just for you. Eat up! It was prepared for this very moment and for these guests.”
Saul ate with Samuel that day. It was pretty epic.
After dinner, they went down from the shrine into the city, and a bed was made for Saul on the cool, breezy roof of Samuel’s house.
At sunrise, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Get up, and I’ll send you off.” Saul got up, and they both went out into the street.
As they were leaving the town, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell your servant to go on ahead. You stay here for a minute. I have a message from God for you.”

title: From Donkey-Finder to King?!
paragraphs: Then Samuel grabbed a flask of oil, poured it right on Saul’s head, and gave him a kiss. He was like, 'Yo, you get what this means, right? God just picked you to be the leader of his people.'

'And to prove God's for real about making you the leader, here's what's gonna happen: After you leave me today and get near your hometown in Benjamin, you're gonna bump into two guys near Rachel's Tomb. They'll tell you, 'Those donkeys you were looking for? They're found. Your dad's not even thinking about the donkeys anymore; he's freaking out about you, like, totally losing it.'

'After that, you'll get to the Oak of Tabor. You'll meet three dudes on their way to worship God at Bethel. One guy will be holding three baby goats, another will have three bags of bread, and the last one will have a jug of wine. They'll be like, 'What's up?' and offer you two loaves of bread. Take them.'

'Then you'll hit Gibeah of God, where a Philistine squad is posted up. As you get close to town, you'll see a whole crew of prophets coming down from the shrine, jamming on harps, tambourines, flutes, and drums. They'll be prophesying like crazy. Then, out of nowhere, God's Spirit will hit you, and you'll start prophesying with them. It's gonna totally change you. You'll be a whole new person.'
'Once all this stuff happens, you'll know you're good to go. Whatever task comes your way, just crush it. God's got your back.'

'Okay, now head down to Gilgal. I'll catch up. I'll come meet you for worship and we'll do some burnt offerings and peace offerings. Just hang tight for seven days. Then I'll show up and tell you the next move.'
As soon as Saul turned to leave Samuel, God just flipped a switch in him—he was a new man. And all those signs Samuel talked about? They all happened that exact same day.

When Saul and his servant got to Gibeah, boom, there was the crew of prophets. Before he could even process it, the Spirit of God came on Saul and he started prophesying right there with them. When people who knew him before saw him prophesying with the prophets, they were shook. 'What is happening? What's gotten into the son of Kish? How in the world is Saul a prophet?' One guy was like, 'Who even are these guys? Where did they come from?'
That's how the saying, 'Saul is one of the prophets now?!' got started. No one saw that coming.
When Saul finished prophesying, he went home. His uncle asked him and his servant, 'So, where have you guys been?'
'Looking for the donkeys. We looked everywhere and couldn't find them. But then we ran into Samuel!'
'Oh yeah?' said Saul's uncle. 'And what did Samuel tell you?'
Saul said, 'He just told us not to worry, the donkeys were found.' But he kept the whole king thing on the down-low, not telling his uncle a single word about it.
Samuel got all the people together to meet God at Mizpah. He told the Israelites, 'This is a personal message from God to you:'

'I'm the one who brought Israel out of Egypt. I saved you from the Egyptians and from all the other powerful governments that were making your lives a living nightmare. And now you're basically ghosting your God, the same God who has a track record of saving you from all kinds of trouble.'
'And now you're like, 'Nah, we want a king! Give us a king!''
'Fine, if that's what you really want, you got it. Line up in front of God by your tribes and families.'

So Samuel got all the tribes of Israel lined up, and the tribe of Benjamin was chosen. Then he had the Benjamin tribe line up by family, and the Matri family was picked. The Matri family got in line, and then Saul, son of Kish, was the name they called. But when they looked for him, he was MIA.
Samuel asked God again, 'Is he even here?'
God said, 'Yep, he's over there, hiding in the luggage.'
They ran and got him. He came and stood in front of everyone, and man, he was tall—like a whole head and shoulders above everyone else.
Samuel then told the people, 'Take a good look at who God has chosen. He's the best! There's no one like him in the whole country!'
Then the crowd went wild, shouting, 'Long live the king!'
Samuel then explained to the people all the rules and responsibilities of having a king, wrote it all down in a book, and put it in a sacred place before God. Then Samuel sent everyone home.

Saul went home to Gibeah, and a squad of legit brave guys, whose hearts God had touched, went with him. But some sketchy dudes were just hating in the corner, muttering, 'This guy is gonna save us? Yeah, right.' They totally dissed him and didn't even say congrats. But Saul just ignored them.

Nahash, the king of the Ammonites, was being a total bully to the tribes of Gad and Reuben, poking out their right eyes and scaring off anyone who tried to help Israel. Pretty much every Israelite on the east side of the Jordan River had their right eye poked out by Nahash. But seven thousand guys had escaped the Ammonites and were now hiding out safely in Jabesh.

title: The King's First BIG W
paragraphs: So this dude Nahash decided to go after the people of Jabesh Gilead and was ready to throw down. The folks in Jabesh were shook and basically begged him, “Hey, let’s make a deal. We’ll totally serve you.”

But Nahash was on a power trip and said, “I’ll make a treaty, but on one condition: I get to gouge out every single one of your right eyes. I’m about to make all of Israel look like a joke before I’m done.”
The town leaders in Jabesh were like, “Whoa, hold up. Give us seven days to send messengers across Israel. If nobody comes to save us, fine, we’ll agree to your messed-up terms.”
So the messengers rushed to Saul’s hometown, Gibeah, and told everyone what was happening. The people just started weeping like crazy. Right then, Saul strolls in from the fields with his oxen.
Saul’s like, “What’s wrong? Why is everyone crying?”
And they told him the grim news from Jabesh.

The moment Saul heard it, the Spirit of God just rushed over him and he went into a legit rage. He grabbed a pair of his oxen, butchered them, and sent the pieces all over Israel with this message: “Anyone who doesn’t ride out with Saul and Samuel, this is what’s gonna happen to your oxen.” It was intense.
God put a major fear into the people, and they all showed up, every single one of them. Saul gathered them at Bezek. There were 300,000 guys from Israel and another 30,000 from Judah. A whole army.
Saul told the messengers, “Go tell the people in Jabesh Gilead: ‘Help is coming. By noon tomorrow, you’ll be saved.’”

The messengers booked it back and delivered the good news. The people of Jabesh were so hyped. They sent a message to Nahash, saying, “Tomorrow, we’ll surrender, and you can do whatever you want with us.” But it was a total fake-out. Long before sunrise the next day, Saul had his army split into three groups. At the crack of dawn, they ambushed the enemy camp and just wrecked the Ammonites until noon. The survivors scattered, running for their lives in every direction.
After that, the people went to Samuel and were like, “Where are those guys who were saying, ‘Saul can’t be our king’? Bring them here. We’re gonna kill them!”
But Saul, showing some real class, said, “Nah, nobody’s getting executed today. Today is the day God saved Israel! Come on, let’s all go to Gilgal and make this king thing official again.”
So everyone went to Gilgal. There, in front of God, they crowned Saul as king. They sacrificed peace offerings and had a massive celebration. Saul and all of Israel were on top of the world.

title: Samuel's Mic Drop: You REALLY Wanted a King?
paragraphs: Samuel hit up all of Israel and was like, “Alright, I listened to every single thing you said, and I gave you a king. Now look, your king is leading you. But look at me—I'm old and gray, and my sons are still around. I've led you guys faithfully since I was young until today. So for real, look at me. You got any complaints to bring to God and his new king? Have I ever stolen an ox or a donkey? Have I ever taken advantage of you or exploited you? Have I ever taken a bribe or been shady with the law? Bring it on, and I'll make it right.”
They were all like, “Oh no, never. You’ve never done any of that—never abused us, never lined your own pockets.”
“Okay, bet,” said Samuel. “God is my witness, and his anointed king is my witness, that you can't find anything on me—no faults, no complaints.”
And the people said, “He is witness.”

Samuel went on, “This is the same God who appointed Moses and Aaron and brought your ancestors out of Egypt. So stand here before Him while I lay out the receipts before God, showing all the legit ways He's worked with you and your ancestors. When Jacob’s sons went to Egypt, the Egyptians made life miserable for them, and they cried out to God for help. So God sent Moses and Aaron, who led your ancestors out of Egypt and settled them in this very place.

“But they just forgot their God, so He sold them off to Sisera, the commander of Hazor’s army, then to a rough life under the Philistines, and later to the king of Moab. They had to fight for their lives.

“Then they cried out to God again, confessing, ‘We messed up! We left God and started worshiping the fertility gods and goddesses of Canaan. Please, save us from our enemies, and we’ll worship you and only you.’
“So God sent Jerub-Baal (a.k.a. Gideon), Bedan (a.k.a. Barak), Jephthah, and me, Samuel. He saved you from all your enemies, and you were able to live in peace.
“But the moment you saw Nahash, the Ammonite king, coming to attack, you told me, ‘Nah, we're done with this. We want a king to lead us.’ And this whole time, God was already your king!

“So here’s the king you wanted, the one you begged for. God let you have your way and gave you a king. If you fear God, worship and obey Him, and don't rebel against what He says—if both you and your king follow God, then it's all good. God will for sure save you. But if you don’t obey Him and rebel against His commands, king or no king, you're gonna get wrecked just like your ancestors.

“Now pay attention! Watch this wild thing God is about to do right in front of you. It’s summer, you know, the rainy season is over. But I’m about to pray to God, and He’ll send thunder and rain as a sign to prove what a huge mistake you made in God's eyes by asking for a king.”
Samuel prayed to God, and that same day, God sent thunder and rain. The people were totally freaked out and in awe of God and Samuel.
Then all the people begged Samuel, “Pray to your God for us, your servants! Pray that we don’t die! On top of all our other sins, we added another one—asking for a king!”

Samuel told them, “Don't be scared. It's true you did something really wrong. But still, don't turn your back on God. Worship and serve him with your whole heart. Don’t go chasing after fake gods. They're literally nothing. They can't help you. They're just ghosts. God isn't going to just abandon His people, just because of who He is. God was actually stoked to make you His own people.

“And I'm not going to abandon you either. That would be a sin against God! I’m staying right here at my post, praying for you and teaching you the good and right way to live. But I'm begging you, fear God and worship Him for real, with all your heart. You’ve seen the amazing things He's done for you! But be warned: if you keep messing up, both you and your king will be kicked to the curb.”

title: Saul's Big Mistake & Getting Fired by God
paragraphs: Saul was pretty young when he became king, and he ruled over Israel for a long time.
Saul rounded up enough guys for three squads. He kept two with him at Micmash and in the Bethel hills. The third squad was with his son Jonathan at Gibeah in Benjamin. Everyone else, he sent home.

Jonathan went and took out the Philistine governor who was posted up at Geba (Gibeah). When the Philistines heard about it, they freaked out, like, 'The Hebrews are rebelling!' So Saul had the trumpets sound off everywhere. The news spread all over Israel: 'Saul took out the Philistine governor—he threw the first punch! The Philistines are totally ticked off and ready to fight.' The army was called up and met Saul at Gilgal.

The Philistines gathered their army to fight Israel: three companies of chariots, six companies of cavalry, and so many soldiers on foot they looked like sand on a beach. They went up into the hills and set up their camp at Micmash, east of Beth Aven.

When the Israelites saw they were seriously outnumbered and in a tight spot, they bolted. They hid out in caves, holes in the ground, cliffs, bushes, and even old wells—anywhere they could find. They crossed the Jordan River, running for their lives to the land of Gad and Gilead. But Saul stayed put in Gilgal, and the soldiers who were still with him were shaking in their boots.
He waited for seven days, which was the time Samuel had set. But Samuel was a no-show at Gilgal, and Saul's soldiers started deserting him left and right.

So Saul just took over. 'Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings!' he said. And he went and did the burnt offering himself. Right after he finished, Samuel finally showed up. Saul went to greet him.
Samuel was like, 'What in the world are you doing?'

Saul explained, 'I saw my army slipping away, you didn't come when you said you would, and the Philistines were all ready to attack at Micmash. I thought, 'The Philistines are about to roll up on me here in Gilgal, and I haven't even asked God for help yet.' So I felt like I had to do something, and I sacrificed the burnt offering.'

'That was a really dumb move,' Samuel told Saul. 'If you had just followed the command your God gave you, God would have made your kingdom last forever in Israel. But now, your kingdom is already crumbling. God is already searching for your replacement—the kind of guy who's after God's own heart. He's going to pick him himself. When He finds him, He'll make him the leader of His people. And it's all because you couldn't keep your appointment with God!'

After that, Samuel got up and left Gilgal. What was left of the army followed Saul into battle. They went from Gilgal up to Gibeah in Benjamin. Saul did a headcount of the soldiers still with him—only about six hundred guys!

Saul, his son Jonathan, and the soldiers who were left camped at Geba (Gibeah) in Benjamin. The Philistines were camped at Micmash. The Philistines sent out three raiding parties from their camp. One squad went toward Ophrah in the land of Shual; another went toward Beth Horon; and the third took the road to the border overlooking the Valley of Hyenas.

Back then, you couldn't find a single blacksmith in all of Israel. The Philistines made sure of that, thinking, 'We can't let those Hebrews start making swords and spears.' This meant the Israelites had to go down to the Philistines just to get their farm tools—plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles—sharpened. They charged a silver coin for the big tools and half that for the smaller ones. So when the battle at Micmash started, not a single Israelite soldier had a sword or a spear—except for Saul and his son Jonathan. They were the only ones armed.
A group of Philistine soldiers went and took a position at the Micmash Pass.

title: Jonathan's Sneaky Attack & Saul's Dumb Rule
paragraphs: So, later that day, Saul's son Jonathan was like, "Yo, let's go check out the Philistine patrol on the other side of the pass." But he didn't even tell his dad. Saul was just chilling under a pomegranate tree on the edge of town at Geba (Gibeah) with like 600 guys. Ahijah the priest was there too, wearing the Ephod—he was the son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, son of Phinehas the priest of God at Shiloh, descended from Eli. But yeah, nobody knew Jonathan had bounced.
The pass Jonathan wanted to cross to get to the Philistines had these two huge, sharp rocks on each side, named Bozez and Seneh. One faced Micmash and the other faced Geba (Gibeah).

Jonathan said to his armor bearer, "Aight, let's go deal with these guys who don't even follow God. Maybe God will come in clutch for us. There's no rule that says God can only win with a big army. Literally no one can stop God when He decides to save people."
His armor bearer was like, "Bet. Do what you think is best. I'm with you 100%."

Jonathan said, "Okay, here's the plan. We'll cross over and let them see us. If they're like, 'Freeze! Don't move,' we'll just stay put. But if they say, 'Come on up,' we're going for it—and we'll know God has handed them to us. That's the sign."
So they did it. The two of them just walked out where the Philistine patrol could see them. The Philistines were like, "look! The Hebrews are crawling out of their little holes!"
Then they yelled down to Jonathan and his guy, "Come on up here! We've got something for you!"

Jonathan yelled to his armor bearer, "Let's go! Follow me! God has totally given them to Israel!" Jonathan scrambled up on all fours, and his armor bearer was right behind him. When the Philistines ran at them, Jonathan knocked them down, and his armor bearer finished them off.

In their first fight, Jonathan and his armor bearer took out like twenty guys. This caused total chaos in the Philistine camp and fields. The soldiers and raiding parties were all shook, and the ground was literally shaking—it was a level of panic you've never seen.

Saul's lookouts back in Geba (Gibeah) saw all the chaos in the enemy camp. Saul was like, "Everyone, line up! Take a headcount and see who's missing." When they did, they found out Jonathan and his armor bearer were gone.

Saul told Ahijah, "Bring the priest's Ephod. Let's see what God has to say." (Ahijah was the one in charge of the Ephod back then.) But while Saul was talking to the priest, the chaos in the Philistine camp just got louder and crazier. So Saul was like, "Nvm, put it away."

Saul got his army together and they went straight to the battle. When they got there, it was a hot mess—the Philistines were just swinging their swords everywhere, even killing each other. The Hebrews who had switched to the Philistine side before came back to join Israel under Saul and Jonathan. On top of that, all the Israelites who were hiding in the hills heard the Philistines were running, so they came out and joined the chase. God saved Israel that day! What a day!
The fighting moved on to Beth Aven. The whole army was with Saul now—like ten thousand dudes!—and the fighting spread all over the hills of Ephraim.
But then Saul did something really dumb that day. He told the army, "A curse on anyone who eats anything before tonight, before I get my revenge on my enemies!" So none of them ate anything all day.

There was honeycomb all over the fields. But nobody even touched it, because they were all scared of the curse. But Jonathan hadn't heard his dad's crazy rule. He dipped the end of his staff in some honey and ate it. He instantly felt refreshed, his eyes lit up.
One of the soldiers was like, "Uh, your dad made the whole army swear not to eat anything today. That's why everyone's so tired."

Jonathan said, "My dad just messed up the whole country. Look how much better I feel after just a little honey! It would've been way better if the soldiers had eaten the food they took from the enemy. Who knows how many more we could've beaten!"

They were taking out Philistines all the way from Micmash to Aijalon, but the soldiers were completely wiped. Then they just started grabbing whatever they could—sheep, cattle, calves—and butchered them right there. They just started stuffing their faces—meat, blood, everything.
Someone told Saul, "The soldiers are sinning against God! They're eating meat with the blood still in it!"

Saul said, "You're messing up! Roll a big rock over here—now!" He then said, "Go tell the troops, 'Bring your animals to me and butcher them here the right way. Then you can eat all you want. But don't sin against God by eating meat with blood in it.'"
So they all did that. That night, every soldier brought their animal to be butchered there.
That's how Saul built his first altar to God.
Saul said, "Let's go after the Philistines tonight! We can just keep looting them. We won't leave a single one alive!"
The troops were like, "Sounds good to us, let's do it!"
But the priest was like, "Hold up, let's see what God thinks first."
So Saul prayed to God, "Should I go after the Philistines? Will you give them to us?" But God didn't answer him that time.
Saul then said, "All officers, step up. Someone sinned today. We're gonna find out who it is! I swear by God, Israel's Savior, whoever sinned will die, even if it's my own son, Jonathan!"
Nobody said a word.
Saul told the Israelites, "You guys stand on that side, and me and my son Jonathan will stand on this side."
The army was like, "Fine, whatever you say."

Then Saul prayed to God, "God of Israel, why didn't you answer me today? Show me the truth. If the sin is with me or Jonathan, give the Urim sign. But if the sin is with the army, give the Thummim sign."
The Urim sign came up, pointing to Saul and Jonathan. So the army was cleared.
Next Saul said, "Now cast the lots between me and Jonathan—and the one God points to will die!"
The soldiers were like, "No—this is messed up. Stop!" But Saul didn't listen. They cast the lots, Urim and Thummim, and it landed on Jonathan.
Saul confronted Jonathan. "What did you do? Tell me!"
Jonathan said, "I just tasted a little bit of honey from my staff. That's it—and I'm supposed to die for that?"
Saul said, "Yep. Jonathan will die. It's out of my hands—I can't go against God, right?"

The soldiers all stood up and said, "Jonathan? Die? No way! He just got this huge win for Israel. As long as God is alive, not a single hair on his head will be touched. He was working with God all day!" So the soldiers saved Jonathan, and he didn't die.
Saul stopped chasing the Philistines, and the Philistines went home.

Saul took over and expanded his kingdom. He fought enemies on every side—Moab, Ammon, Edom, the king of Zobah, the Philistines. Everywhere he went, he won. He was basically invincible. He even crushed Amalek, saving Israel from all their attacks.

Saul's sons were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malki-Shua. His daughters were Merab, the oldest, and Michal, the younger one. Saul's wife was Ahinoam, daughter of Ahimaaz. Abner was the commander of his army (and also Saul's cousin). Saul's dad was Kish, and Abner's dad was Ner—both of them sons of Abiel.
Saul's whole life was just one long, brutal war with the Philistines. He would recruit any strong and brave guy he saw.

title: King Saul's Epic Fail
paragraphs: Samuel told Saul, "Yo, God sent me to make you king over His people, Israel. So for real, you gotta listen to what God's saying now. This is the God of the Angel Armies talking:

'I'm about to give Amalek some serious payback for ambushing Israel when they were coming up from Egypt. So here's the plan: Go mess up Amalek. Everything they have? It's all gotta go. No exceptions. This is total destruction—men, women, kids, babies, cows, sheep, camels, donkeys—everything.'
Saul got the army together at Telaim and prepped them for war—two hundred squads of soldiers from Israel and another ten from Judah. Saul marched to Amalek City and hid out in the canyon.

Then Saul sent a message to the Kenites: "You guys need to bounce. Get out of the city ASAP or you're gonna get caught up in this mess with the Amalekites. I'm warning you 'cause you were actually cool to the Israelites when they came up from Egypt."
And they dipped. The Kenites got out of there.

Then Saul went after Amalek, from the canyon all the way to Shur near Egypt. He captured King Agag of Amalek alive. Everyone else was taken out, just like the plan said. But Saul and the army decided to keep Agag and the best sheep and cattle. They didn't count them in the total wipeout. But all the other stuff that nobody really wanted, they destroyed like they were supposed to.
Then God hit up Samuel: "I'm honestly sorry I ever made Saul king. He's totally turned his back on me. He won't do what I tell him."

Samuel was mad when he heard this. He spent the whole night praying through his anger and disappointment. He got up early to go find Saul but someone told him, "Saul's gone. He went to Carmel to build a monument to himself for his 'victory,' and then he was heading to Gilgal."
By the time Samuel found him, Saul had just finished a worship service, using the stuff he took from the Amalekites for the offerings to God.
When Samuel got close, Saul yelled out, "God bless you! I followed God's plan perfectly!"
Samuel was like, "Then what's all this I'm hearing—the sound of sheep and cows?"
"Oh, just some stuff from the Amalekites," Saul said. "The soldiers saved the best cattle and sheep to sacrifice to God. But we destroyed everything else, for real."
"Stop talking!" Samuel cut him off. "Let me tell you what God told me last night."
Saul said, "Okay, fine. Tell me."

And Samuel laid it all out. "When you first started, you were a nobody—and you knew it. Then God made you the leader of Israel—king over Israel. Then God gave you a mission, telling you, 'Go and completely wipe out those sinners, the Amalekites. Fight them until they're all gone.' So why didn't you listen to God? Why'd you just grab all their stuff? Why, when God was watching you the whole time, did you do something so messed up?"

Saul tried to defend himself. "What are you talking about? I did listen to God. I did the mission He gave me. I brought back King Agag and destroyed the Amalekites like I was supposed to. The soldiers just saved a few of the best sheep and cattle to sacrifice to God at Gilgal—what's the big deal?"
Then Samuel said,

"You think all God wants are sacrifices—just empty rituals? He wants you to actually listen to Him! Just listening is the main thing, not putting on some big religious show. Not doing what God tells you is way worse than messing with black magic. Thinking you're all that in front of God is worse than trying to talk to ghosts. Because you said 'nah' to God's command, He's saying 'nah' to you being king."

Saul finally caved and confessed, "I messed up. I totally ignored God's Word and what you said. I was more worried about what the people thought. I let them boss me around. Please, forgive my sin! Take my hand and lead me to the altar so I can worship God!"
But Samuel was like, "No, I can't do that with you. You rejected God's command. Now God has rejected you as king over Israel."

As Samuel turned to leave, Saul grabbed his robe and a piece of it ripped off. Samuel said, "God just ripped the kingdom away from you, right now, and gave it to your neighbor, someone who's a better man than you. The glorious God of Israel doesn't lie and He doesn't change His mind. He means what He says."
Saul tried again, "I know I sinned. But don't just leave me like this! Stand by me in front of the leaders and the people. Come with me while I go back to worship God—this time, God, my God."
So Samuel did. He went back with him. And Saul got on his knees before God and worshiped.
Then Samuel said, "Bring me King Agag of Amalek." Agag came, dragging his feet, mumbling that he'd rather be dead.
Samuel said, "Just like your sword made a bunch of moms lose their kids, now your mom is gonna be one of them." And Samuel took down Agag right there in front of God at Gilgal.

Samuel left for Ramah right after that, and Saul went home to Gibeah. Samuel didn't have anything to do with Saul after that, even though he was super sad about him for a long time. But God was sorry He ever made Saul king in the first place.

title: God's Secret New King Pick
paragraphs: God hit up Samuel and was like, “So, how long are you gonna mope about Saul? You know I’ve kicked him out of being king over Israel. Fill up your flask with anointing oil and get going. I’m sending you to this guy Jesse in Bethlehem. I’ve found the king I want, and he’s one of his sons.”
“I can’t do that,” Samuel said. “Saul will hear about it and literally kill me.”

God was like, “Just take a heifer with you and say, ‘I’ve come to worship God, and this heifer is the sacrifice.’ Make sure Jesse gets an invite. I’ll tell you what to do from there. I’ll point out the one you need to anoint.”
So Samuel did what God told him. When he got to Bethlehem, the town elders came out to meet him, looking pretty nervous. “Is everything cool?” they asked.

“Everything’s cool. I’m here to sacrifice this heifer and lead you in the worship of God. Get yourselves ready, get consecrated, and come worship with me.” He also made sure Jesse and his sons got consecrated and were invited to worship.
When they showed up, Samuel took one look at Eliab and thought, “Yo, this has to be him! God’s anointed one!”

But God told Samuel, “Don’t just look at his face or how tall he is. I’ve already passed on him. God doesn’t see things the way people do. People judge by what they see on the outside, but God looks at the heart.”
Then Jesse called up Abinadab and had him meet Samuel. Samuel was like, “Nope, this isn’t God’s pick either.”
Next, Jesse brought out Shammah. Samuel said, “Nah, not this guy either.”
Jesse introduced all seven of his sons to Samuel. Samuel was straight up with Jesse, “God hasn’t picked any of these guys.”
Then he asked Jesse, “Is that everyone? You don’t have any more sons?”
“Well, yeah, there’s the youngest. But he’s out watching the sheep.”
Samuel told Jesse, “Go get him. We’re not going anywhere until he’s here.”
Jesse sent for him. They brought him in, and he was looking healthy, with bright eyes and super good-looking.
God said, “Get up! Anoint him! This is the one.”
Samuel grabbed his flask of oil and anointed him right there in front of his brothers. The Spirit of God rushed over David like a gust of wind, giving him major power for the rest of his life.
Samuel then bounced and went home to Ramah.
At that exact moment, the Spirit of God left Saul, and instead, this dark mood sent by God just settled over him. He was totally freaked out.

Saul’s advisors were like, “This awful, tormenting evil spirit from God is making your life a nightmare. Sir, let us help. We can find someone who can play the harp. When that evil spirit from God comes over you, he’ll play his music, and you’ll feel better.”
Saul told his servants, “Alright, do it. Find me someone who’s a good musician and bring him to me.”

One of the young guys spoke up, “I know a guy. I’ve seen him myself: he’s the son of Jesse from Bethlehem, and he’s an amazing musician. He’s also brave, old enough, speaks well, and is good-looking. Plus, God is with him.”
So Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, “Send me your son David, the one who takes care of the sheep.”

Jesse got a donkey, loaded it up with some bread, a flask of wine, and a young goat, and sent his son David with it to Saul. David came to Saul and stood before him. Saul instantly liked him and made him his right-hand man.
Saul sent a message back to Jesse: “Thanks. David’s staying here. He’s exactly who I was looking for. I’m super impressed by him.”
After that, whenever the evil spirit from God would come on Saul, David would take out his harp and play. It would calm Saul down, and he’d feel better as the evil spirit left him.

title: David vs. Goliath: The Ultimate Showdown
paragraphs: So the Philistines got their squad ready for a fight. They set up at Socoh in Judah, camping between Socoh and Azekah at a place called Ephes Dammim. Saul and the Israelites linked up, made camp in Oak Valley, and got in formation, ready to take on the Philistines. The Philistines were on one hill, the Israelites on the hill across from them, with a whole valley in between.

Then this absolute unit, a giant who was almost ten feet tall, stepped out from the Philistine line. It was Goliath from Gath. He had a bronze helmet on and was decked out in armor that weighed, like, 126 pounds! He had on bronze shin guards and was carrying a bronze sword. His spear was massive, like a fence rail, and the spearhead alone was over fifteen pounds. He even had a guy walking in front of him just to carry his shield.

Goliath just stood there and yelled over to the Israelite army, “Why are you even bothering to bring out your whole army? Aren't I enough? And you're all Team Saul, right? So just pick your best fighter and let him fight me. If he wins and takes me out, we Philistines will be your slaves. But if I win and take him out, you'll all be our slaves and work for us. I'm calling out the army of Israel today. Send me a man. Let's settle this one-on-one!”
When Saul and his troops heard what the Philistine said, they were seriously freaked out and felt totally hopeless.

But then, David shows up. He was the son of Jesse, an Ephrathite from Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons and was too old to join Saul's army himself. His three oldest sons had gone off to war with Saul. The three who went were Eliab, the oldest; Abinadab, the second; and Shammah, the third. David was the youngest. While his three older brothers were with Saul at the war, David was going back and forth between helping Saul and taking care of his dad's sheep in Bethlehem.
For forty days, Goliath would come out every morning and evening and give his little speech.

One day, Jesse told his son David, “Take this bag of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread and run them over to your brothers at the camp. And take these ten blocks of cheese to their captain. See how your brothers are doing, and bring me back some kind of proof that they're okay. You know, with Saul and your brothers and all the Israelites fighting the Philistines in Oak Valley.”

David got up super early, found someone to watch the sheep, grabbed the food, and headed out just like Jesse told him. He got to the camp right as the army was moving into their battle lines, shouting their war cry. Israel and the Philistines were getting into position, facing off, ready to fight. David left his stuff with a guard, ran to the battle lines, and said hi to his brothers. While they were catching up, the Philistine champion, Goliath of Gath, stepped out from the Philistine lines and made his usual challenge. David heard it all.

The Israelite soldiers, every single one of them, backed away as soon as they saw the giant. They were completely terrified. The buzz among the soldiers was, “Can you believe this guy, openly dissing Israel like this? Whoever kills this giant is gonna be set for life. The king will give him a massive reward, his daughter's hand in marriage, and his whole family will be tax-free.”

David, talking to the guys standing around, asked, “So, what’s the prize for the guy who takes out that Philistine and ends this major embarrassment for Israel? I mean, who does this uncircumcised Philistine think he is, taunting the armies of the living God?”
They just repeated what everyone else was saying about the king's reward for the guy who kills him.

Eliab, his older brother, heard David chatting with the soldiers and got super mad. “What are you even doing here? Why aren't you at home watching those few sheep of yours? I know your game. You just came down here to watch the action, hoping to get a front-row seat to a bloody fight!”
“Whoa, what's your problem?” David shot back. “I just asked a question.” He ignored his brother, turned to someone else, asked the same thing, and got the same story.
Word got back to Saul about what David was saying, so Saul sent for him.
“Don't lose hope, sir,” David said. “I'm ready to go fight this Philistine.”
Saul replied, “You can't go fight him. You're just a kid, you've got no experience. This guy has been a warrior since he was young.”

David said, “I've been a shepherd for my father. Whenever a lion or a bear came and tried to snatch a lamb from the flock, I'd go after it, beat it up, and rescue the lamb. If it turned on me, I'd grab it by the jaw, and finish it off. Lion or bear, didn't matter—I killed it. And I'll do the same thing to this pagan Philistine who's been dissing the armies of the living God. The same God who saved me from the lion's teeth and the bear's claws will save me from this Philistine.”
Saul said, “Go. And may God be with you.”
Then Saul tried to suit David up in his own armor. He put a bronze helmet on his head and strapped his sword on him over the armor. David tried to walk, but he could barely even move.
David told Saul, “I can't move with all this gear on. I'm not used to it.” So he took it all off.
Then David grabbed his shepherd's staff, picked out five smooth stones from a stream, put them in his shepherd's bag, and with his sling in his hand, he went to face Goliath.
As the Philistine, with his shield-carrier in front, walked back and forth, he saw David. He looked down at him and just scoffed—a young, fresh-faced kid.
The Philistine dissed David, “Am I a dog, that you’re coming at me with a stick?” And he cursed him in the name of his gods.
“Come on over here,” said the Philistine. “I'll make roadkill out of you for the buzzards. You'll be a tasty little snack for the field mice.”

David shot back, “You come at me with a sword and a spear and a javelin, but I come at you in the name of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, who you've been mocking. Today, God is going to hand you over to me. I'm going to kill you, cut off your head, and feed your dead body and the bodies of your Philistine buddies to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know there's a God in Israel. And everyone here will see that God doesn't need a sword or a spear to save people. The battle is the Lord's, and he's about to hand you over to us.”

That got the Philistine moving, and he started coming toward David. David ran from the front line to meet him. He reached into his bag for a stone, put it in his sling, and slung it right at the Philistine's forehead. The stone sank deep into his forehead, and the Philistine fell flat on his face.
And that's how David beat the Philistine—with a sling and a stone. He struck him down and killed him. David didn't even have a sword!

Then David ran over, stood over the Philistine, took the giant's own sword from its sheath, and finished him off by cutting off his head. When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they freaked out and ran for it.

The men of Israel and Judah jumped up, shouting, and chased the Philistines all the way to the edge of Gath and the gates of Ekron. The road to Shaaraim was littered with wounded Philistines all the way to Gath and Ekron. After chasing them, the Israelites came back and took all the stuff from their camp. David took the Philistine's head to Jerusalem, but he put the giant's weapons in his own tent.
When Saul saw David going out to fight the Philistine, he asked Abner, the commander of his army, “Hey, who's this kid's dad?” Abner said, “Honestly, O King, I have no idea.”
Abner said, “I swear, Your Majesty, I have no idea.”
The king said, “Well, find out who this young guy's family is.”
As soon as David came back from killing the Philistine, Abner brought him straight to Saul. David was still holding the Philistine's head.
Saul asked him, “Young man, who's your father?” And David answered, “I'm the son of your servant Jesse—the one who lives in Bethlehem.”
And David answered, “I'm the son of your servant Jesse, from Bethlehem.”

title: From Best Bro to Worst Enemy
paragraphs: By the time David was done talking to Saul, Jonathan was totally blown away by him—they had this instant connection. He was all in on David, becoming his number one supporter and friend from that moment on.
That same day, Saul brought David into his own house, and he didn't go back to his dad's place anymore.
Jonathan, because he cared for David so much, made a serious promise with him. He made it official by giving him some big-deal gifts: his own royal robe and all his gear—armor, sword, bow, and belt.

Whatever Saul asked David to do, he crushed it. He was so good that Saul put him in charge of the army. Everyone, from the regular folks to Saul's own officials, thought David was an awesome leader and totally respected him.

On their way back home after David took down the Philistine, women came out from all the towns in Israel, singing and dancing to welcome King Saul with tambourines, party songs, and lutes. The women were joking around and sang,
'Saul kills by the thousand, David by the ten thousand!'

This made Saul furious—like, really mad. He felt like they were dissing him personally. He was like, “They’re giving David credit for ‘ten thousands’ and I only get ‘thousands.’ Next thing you know, they’ll be making him the king!” From that day on, Saul was super suspicious of David.

The next day, God sent this nasty mood to mess with Saul, and he totally lost it, just raving, totally out of control. David started playing his harp, like he usually did when Saul got like this. Saul was holding a spear, and then all of a sudden, he threw it, thinking, “I’m gonna pin David to the wall.” But David dodged it, and the spear missed. This happened two times.

After that, Saul was scared of David. It was obvious that God was with David and had bounced on Saul. So, Saul got David out of his face by making him an officer in the army. David was out fighting all the time. Everything David did was a success. For real, God was with him. The more Saul saw David winning, the more scared he got. He knew it was over for him. But everyone else in Israel and Judah loved David. They loved seeing him in action.

One day Saul said to David, “Check it out, here’s Merab, my oldest daughter. I want to give her to you as your wife. Just be a beast for me and fight God’s battles!” But really, Saul was thinking, “The Philistines will take him out for me. I won’t even have to do anything.”
David was super humbled and was like, “Are you for real? My family is a bunch of nobodies! I can’t be the king’s son-in-law.”
The wedding day was all set, but when it was almost time for Merab and David to get married, Saul bailed and married her off to some other guy, Adriel the Meholathite.

But get this, Saul’s other daughter, Michal, had a major crush on David. When Saul heard about it, he was totally scheming. “Yes, a second chance. I’ll use Michal as bait to get David right where the Philistines can finish him off.” So he said to David again, “You’re gonna be my son-in-law after all.”
Saul told his servants, “Go talk to David privately and tell him, ‘The king is a big fan of yours, and everyone at court thinks you’re great. Just do it, become the king’s son-in-law!’”
The king’s servants told David all this, but David was still hesitant. “What are you guys talking about? I can’t do that. I’m a nobody; I’ve got nothing to bring to the table.”

When the servants told Saul what David said, he told them to tell David this: “The king doesn’t want any cash from you; just this: Go kill a hundred Philistines and bring back the proof. Get revenge for the king on his enemies.” (Saul was pretty sure David would get killed trying to do this.)

When David got this message, he was actually stoked. There was finally something he could do for the king that would make him worthy of being his son-in-law! He didn’t waste any time. He and his guys went right out, killed a hundred Philistines, brought back the evidence in a bag, and counted it all out for the king—mission accomplished! So Saul gave his daughter Michal to David as his wife.
As Saul started to realize more and more that God was with David, and saw how much his own daughter, Michal, loved him, his fear of David grew and turned into straight-up hate. Saul hated David.
Whenever the Philistine bosses came out for a fight, David was there to shut them down, totally showing up Saul’s own guys. David’s name was literally on everyone’s lips.

title: David's Wild Escape from a Psycho King
paragraphs: Saul told his son Jonathan and all his officials to straight up kill David. But Jonathan was tight with David, so he went and gave him a heads-up: “My dad is literally trying to find a way to kill you. So here’s the plan. Tomorrow morning, you need to disappear and stay completely hidden. I’ll go out with my dad to the field where you’re hiding. I’ll bring you up in conversation and see what he says. Then I’ll tell you everything.”

Jonathan went to his dad and talked David up, saying, “Dad, please don’t do David dirty like that. He’s never done anything to you, has he? And look at all the awesome stuff he’s done! He put his life on the line to kill that Philistine. God gave Israel a huge win that day! You were there. You saw it and you were cheering louder than anyone. So why would you even think about sinning against an innocent guy and killing David for no reason?”
Saul actually listened to Jonathan and said, “You’re right. As God is real, David will live. He will not be killed.”
So Jonathan called David and told him everything they said. Then he brought David back to Saul, and things were cool again, just like before.
But then war broke out again, and David went to fight the Philistines. He totally wrecked them, and they all ran away scared.

Then, this dark mood sent by God settled on Saul and took over. He was just sitting at home, holding his spear, while David was playing some music. Suddenly, Saul tried to pin David to the wall with his spear, but David ducked. The spear got stuck in the wall, and David bounced. This all went down at night.

Saul sent guys to David’s house to watch it and then kill him first thing in the morning. But Michal, David’s wife, told him what was up. “You have to escape tonight. If you don’t, you’ll be dead by morning!” She let him down from a window, and he got away. Then Michal grabbed a household idol, put it in the bed, put a wig made of goat’s hair on its head, and threw a blanket over it. When Saul’s guys showed up to grab David, she said, “He’s sick in bed.”
Saul sent his guys back, ordering them, “Bring him to me, bed and all, so I can kill him myself.” When the men went into the room, all they found in the bed was the idol with the goat-hair wig!
Saul was so mad at Michal: “How could you trick me like this? You took my enemy’s side, and now he’s gone!”
Michal shot back, “He threatened me. He said, ‘Help me get out of here or I’ll kill you.’”
David got away and went to Samuel at Ramah and told him everything Saul had done. Then he and Samuel bounced to a private place called Naioth.

Someone told Saul, “David’s at Naioth in Ramah.” He immediately sent his men to capture him. But when they got there, they saw a group of prophets prophesying, with Samuel leading them. Before they knew it, the Spirit of God came on them too, and they started prophesying and going wild right along with them!
Someone told Saul what happened, so he sent more men. They also started prophesying. So Saul tried a third time with a third group of men—and they ended up doing the same thing!
Saul was so over it, he went to Ramah himself. He got to the big well at Secu and asked, “Where are Samuel and David?”
A random person said, “Over at Naioth in Ramah.”

As he was heading to Naioth in Ramah, the Spirit of God came on him, too. The whole way there, he kept prophesying, too. He stripped off his clothes and lay there prophesying in front of Samuel for a whole day and a night, completely naked. People still talk about it, saying, “Is Saul a prophet now too? Who would’ve thought?”

title: My Best Friend's Dad Wants Me Dead
paragraphs: David managed to get out of Naioth in Ramah and went straight to Jonathan, asking, "Yo, what do I do? What did I do to your dad that has him so set on killing me?"

"Nothing," Jonathan replied. "You've done zero wrong. And you're not going to die, for real. My dad tells me everything, big or small, he doesn't do anything without telling me. So why would he keep this from me? No way."

But David was like, "Look, your dad knows we're best friends. So he's probably thinking, 'Jonathan can't know about this, or he'll take David's side.' But I'm telling you, as sure as God is real and you're standing here, he's dead serious about killing me."
Jonathan said, "Just tell me what you're thinking. I'll do anything for you."

David laid out the plan: "Okay, so tomorrow is the New Moon festival, and I'm supposed to have dinner with the king. But instead, I'm gonna go hide in a field until the third evening. If your dad even notices I'm gone, just say, 'David really wanted to go back to his hometown, Bethlehem, for a family thing.' If he's cool with it and says, 'Good!' then I know I'm safe. But if he gets mad, you'll know for sure he's planning to kill me. Please, stick with me on this. We made a pact before God, remember? If I'm the one who's wrong, then you can just kill me yourself. Why would you even hand me over to your father?"
