"Never!" Jonathan exclaimed. "I would never do that! If I get even the slightest hint that my dad is serious about killing you, I'll tell you right away."
David then asked, "But who's gonna tell me if your dad gives a harsh answer?"

"Come on, let's go to the field," Jonathan said. When the two of them were out in the field, Jonathan declared, "I swear on God, the God of Israel, that by this time tomorrow, I'll figure out how my dad feels about you. Then I'll let you know what I find out. May God strike me down if I let you down! If my dad still wants to kill you, I'll tell you and get you out of here safely. And may God be with you, just like he was with my father. If I survive this, promise you'll always be my friend. And if I die, promise you'll be friends with my family forever. And when God finally gets rid of all your enemies, stay loyal to me!" Jonathan made his promise to David again, because he loved him more than his own life.

Jonathan then explained his plan: "Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you'll be missed when you don't show up for dinner. On the third day, when they've stopped looking for you, go to the place where you hid before, and wait by that big rock. I'll shoot three arrows toward the rock. Then I'll send my servant to 'Go find the arrows.' If I yell to him, 'The arrows are on this side! Get them!' that's the signal that you can come back safely—I swear, there's nothing to worry about! But if I yell, 'The arrows are farther out!' then you need to run for it—God wants you to get out of here! And about everything we've talked about, just remember that God is in on this with us until the end!"

So David hid in the field. When the New Moon holiday came, the king sat down to eat. He sat in his usual spot against the wall, with Jonathan across from him and Abner next to him. But David's seat was empty. Saul didn't say anything at the time, thinking, "Something must have happened to make him unclean. Yeah, he's probably not clean enough for the holy meal."
But the next day, the second day of the holiday, David's seat was still empty. Saul asked his son Jonathan, "So where's that son of Jesse? He hasn't eaten with us yesterday or today."

Jonathan replied, "David asked for my permission to go to Bethlehem. He said, 'Please let me go to a family reunion back home. My brothers told me I had to be there. If it's cool with you, let me go see my brothers.' That's why he's not at the king's table."

Saul completely lost it and yelled at Jonathan: "You son of a snake! You think I don't know you're on Jesse's son's side, embarrassing both me and your mother? As long as that son of Jesse is alive, you have no future in this kingdom. Now go get him. Bring him here. He's as good as dead!"
Jonathan stood up to his father, asking, "Why should he be dead? What did he do?"
Saul threw his spear at him, trying to kill him. That's when Jonathan knew for sure that his father was determined to kill David.
Jonathan stormed away from the table, super angry, and didn't eat anything for the rest of the day. He was upset for David and hurt by his father's humiliating actions.

In the morning, Jonathan went to the field for his meeting with David, bringing his young servant with him. He told the servant, "Run and get the arrows I'm about to shoot." The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow way past him. When the boy got to where the arrow had landed, Jonathan yelled, "Isn't the arrow farther out?" He yelled again, "Hurry up! Don't just stand there!" The servant then picked up the arrow and brought it to his master. The boy, of course, had no idea what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.

Jonathan gave his bow and arrows to the boy and sent him back to town. After the servant left, David came out from his hiding spot by the rock and bowed down to the ground three times. Then they kissed each other and cried, friend with friend, with David crying the hardest.
Jonathan said, "Go in peace! The two of us have vowed friendship in God's name, saying, 'God will be the bond between us, and between our kids and their kids forever!'"

title: David's Crazy Escape Plan
paragraphs: So David bounced, and Jonathan headed back to the city.
David rolled up to Nob to see Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech was shook when he saw David and was like, 'Yo, why are you here all solo? Where's your crew?'

David told Ahimelech the priest, 'The king sent me on a secret mission, like, super hush-hush. He was like, ‘Don’t tell anyone.’ I’m meeting my guys at a secret spot. Anyway, I’m starving. You got any food? Like five loaves of bread? I’ll take whatever you’ve got.'
'Nah, I don’t have any normal bread,' the priest said. 'Only the holy bread. But if you and your guys haven't been with any girls lately, you can have it.'
David was like, 'Nah, we're good. We haven't been with any women. We always keep it clean on missions. Even on regular ones, so for sure on this holy one.'
So the priest gave him the holy bread. It was all he had. It was the special bread that was put out before God and then swapped out for fresh bread.
One of Saul's guys, this dude named Doeg the Edomite, was there that day doing some religious thing. He was the head of Saul's shepherds.
Then David asked Ahimelech, 'Yo, you got a spear or a sword I can borrow? I had to leave in a rush for the king's mission and didn't have time to grab my weapons.'
The priest said, 'Goliath's sword, the one from the Philistine you killed at Oak Valley—that’s here! It’s behind the Ephod, wrapped in a cloth. If you want it, take it. There’s nothing else here.'
'Oh, sick!' David said. 'There’s no sword like that! Give it to me!'

And just like that, David was out of there, running for his life from Saul. He went to Achish, king of Gath. When Achish's servants saw him, they were like, 'Isn't that David, the famous one? The one they sing about in their dances?'
'Saul kills by the thousand, David by the ten thousand!'

When David realized they knew who he was, he freaked out, scared of what Achish, the king of Gath, would do. So right then and there, while they were all watching, he pretended to be crazy. He started banging his head on the city gate and drooling, with spit dripping down his beard. Achish took one look at him and said to his servants, 'Are you blind? The dude's insane! Why'd you let him in here? You think I don't have enough crazy people to deal with already? Get him out of here!'

title: David's Fugitive Squad & A Royal Meltdown
paragraphs: So David bounced and escaped to the Cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his family heard where he was, they came down and linked up with him. On top of that, everyone who was going through it—people who were broke, in debt, or just fed up—all flocked to him. David became their leader, and he had a crew of about four hundred guys.

From there, David went to Mizpah in Moab and hit up the king, like, 'Yo, can you let my mom and dad crash here with you until I figure out what God's plan is for me?' So he left his parents with the king of Moab, and they stayed there the whole time David was hiding out.
Then the prophet Gad told David, 'Don't stay in the hideout. Get back to the land of Judah.' So David did what he said and went to the forest of Hereth.

Saul got the news that David and his men had been spotted. At the time, Saul was sitting under a big tree on the hill at Gibeah, spear in hand, holding a meeting with his officials. He said, 'Listen up, you Benjaminites! Do you seriously think this son of Jesse is gonna hook you up with fields and vineyards or make you all commanders? You're all plotting against me, and not one of you had the guts to tell me that my own son made a pact with him. None of you care enough to let me know that my son has stirred up my own servant to be an outlaw, waiting to ambush me, which is what's happening now.'

Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing there with Saul's officials, spoke up, 'I saw the son of Jesse go to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub. Ahimelech prayed to God for him, gave him supplies, and even handed him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.'
So Saul sent for the priest Ahimelech son of Ahitub and his whole family, who were all priests at Nob. And they all came to the king.
Saul said, 'Listen here, son of Ahitub!'
'Yes, my king,' he answered.

Saul went off, 'Why did you conspire against me with the son of Jesse? You gave him bread and a sword, and you prayed to God for him, setting him up as an outlaw to ambush me, just like he's doing now!'

Ahimelech replied to the king, 'Literally who among all your servants is as loyal as David? He's the king's son-in-law, captain of your bodyguard, and is crazy respected in your own house. Was this the first time I prayed to God for him? No way. Don't blame me or my family for anything, my king, because your servant has no clue what's going on with all this.'
But the king said, 'You're gonna die, Ahimelech! You and your entire family.'

Then the king ordered the guards at his side, 'Turn and kill the priests of the LORD! They're in on it with David. They knew he was on the run and they didn't tell me.' But the king's officials refused to raise a hand to strike down the LORD's priests.

So the king said to Doeg, 'You do it. Go kill the priests.' So Doeg the Edomite turned and slaughtered them. That day he killed eighty-five men who wore the priest's uniform. He went on to Nob, the city of priests, and wiped it out with the sword—men and women, children and infants, cattle, donkeys, and sheep. A total massacre.
Only one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub, Abiathar, managed to escape and fled to join David. He told David that Saul had murdered the LORD's priests.

David said to Abiathar, 'I knew it that day. When I saw Doeg the Edomite there, I just knew he would snitch to Saul. I'm the one responsible for the deaths of your whole family. Stay with me. Don't be scared. The same person who wants to kill you wants to kill me too. You'll be safe with me.'

title: Narrow Escape
paragraphs: So, word got to David that the Philistines were raiding Keilah and stealing all their grain. David hit up God in prayer, asking, "Yo, should I go after these Philistines and teach them a lesson?"
God was like, "Go. Attack the Philistines and save Keilah."
But David's crew was seriously rattled. They said, "Look, we're already scared for our lives right here in Judah. How can you even think about going to Keilah where it's crawling with Philistines?"
So David went back to God to pray again. God said, "Get going. Head to Keilah. I'm literally placing the Philistines in your hands."

David and his guys went to Keilah and battled the Philistines. He jacked their cattle, totally crushed them, and saved the people of Keilah. After Abiathar bounced to join David, he went with him on the raid, and he even brought the Ephod.

Saul found out that David was in Keilah and immediately thought, "Let's go! God has handed him to me on a silver platter! He's trapped in a walled city with locked gates." Saul gathered his army for battle and headed to Keilah to corner David and his men.

But David got wind of Saul's plan to destroy him and said to Abiathar the priest, "Get the Ephod." Then David prayed to God, "God of Israel, I just heard that Saul is planning to come to Keilah and wreck the city just because of me. Are the city leaders of Keilah gonna turn me over to him? Is Saul really gonna come down and do what I've heard? Oh God, God of Israel, tell me!"
God replied, "He's coming down."
"And are the leaders of Keilah gonna hand me and my men over to Saul?"
And God said, "They'll turn you over."
So David and his men, all 600 of them, got out of there. They left Keilah and just kept it moving, going here, there, wherever—always on the run.
When Saul was told that David had dipped from Keilah, he called off the whole raid.

David kept living in desert hideouts and the wild hills of Ziph. Saul was out looking for him day after day, but God never handed David over to him. David kept a low profile in the wilderness of Ziph, hiding out at Horesh, since it was super obvious that Saul was determined to hunt him down.

Jonathan, Saul's son, visited David at Horesh and encouraged him in God. He said, "Don't even trip. My father, Saul, can't lay a hand on you. You're gonna be Israel's king and I'll be right there by your side to help. And my father knows it, for real." Then the two of them made a pact before God. David stayed at Horesh and Jonathan went home.

Some Ziphites went to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Yo, did you know that David is hiding out near us in the caves and canyons of Horesh? Right now he's at Hakilah Hill just south of Jeshimon. So whenever you're ready to come down, we'd be honored to hand him over to the king."

Saul said, "God bless you for thinking about me! Now go back and check everything out. Learn his whole routine. Watch his movements—where he goes, who he's with. He's super sneaky, you know. Scout out all his hiding spots. Then meet me at Nacon and I'll go with you. If he is anywhere to be found in all of Judah, I'll track him down!"
So the Ziphites set out on their spy mission for Saul.

Meanwhile, David and his men were in the Maon wilderness, in the desert south of Jeshimon. Saul and his men showed up and started their search. When David heard about it, he went south to Rock Mountain and camped out in the Maon wilderness. Saul heard where he was and took off for the Maon wilderness to chase him. Saul was on one side of the mountain, and David and his men were on the other. David was in full retreat, running for his life, with Saul and his men closing in, about to catch him. But just then, a messenger came to Saul and said, "Hurry! Come back! The Philistines just attacked the country!"

So Saul called off his chase of David and went back to deal with the Philistines. That's how that place got the name 'Narrow Escape.' David left there and camped out in the caves and canyons of En Gedi.

title: Cave Showdown: David's Big Mercy Play
paragraphs: So, Saul gets back from fighting the Philistines, and someone's like, "Yo, David's hiding out in the En Gedi wilderness." Saul took three companies—the best he could find, 3,000 of Israel's top soldiers—and headed out to the Wild Goat Rocks area to find David and his crew.

He gets to these sheep pens on the side of the road, and there's a cave. Saul goes inside for a bathroom break. And guess what? David and his guys were hiding way in the back of that exact same cave. David's men were whispering to him, "Bro, no way. This is the day God was talking about. He promised He'd put your enemy in your hands and you could do whatever you want with him." So David, quiet as a ninja, creeps up and snips off a corner of Saul's royal robe.

But instantly, he felt super guilty about it. He told his men, "God forbid I would do something like this to my king, the one God himself chose. I can't even lift a finger against him. He's God's anointed!" David shut his men down with that and stopped them from attacking Saul. Saul got up, walked out of the cave, and went on his way.

Then David went to the entrance of the cave and shouted after Saul, "My king! My master!" Saul looked back, and David dropped to his knees and bowed down. He yelled out, "Why do you even listen to people who say I'm out to get you? Today, you saw it with your own eyes. God literally handed you to me in that cave. My guys wanted to kill you, but I said no. I told them I wouldn't touch my king—because he's the one God anointed. Look, my father, look at this piece of your robe in my hand. I cut this off instead of killing you! See the proof? I'm not trying to overthrow you. I'm not a traitor. I haven't done anything wrong to you, but you're still hunting me down to kill me. Let God decide who's right here. God can get revenge for me, but I'm not going to do it myself. There's an old saying, 'Evil deeds come from evil people,' so you can be sure I'll never lay a hand on you.

"Who is the king of Israel even chasing? A dead dog? A single flea? God is the judge. He'll see the situation and decide what's right. I just pray He'll look at my case and get me out of this mess with you!"

When David finished his speech, Saul started sobbing and said, "Is that really your voice, my son David?" He cried his eyes out. "You're the one in the right, not me," he said. "You've been good to me while I've been awful to you. And you just proved it again—you were so generous. God put me in your hands, and you didn't kill me. I mean, who finds their enemy and just sends them off with a blessing? May God bless you like crazy for what you did for me today! Now I know, for real, that you're going to be the king. The kingdom of Israel is basically yours already. Just promise me, swear to God, that you won't wipe out my family or erase my name from history."
David made the promise to Saul. Then Saul went home, and David and his men went back up to their hideout.

title: David vs. The Rich Fool: How One Woman Prevented a Bloodbath
paragraphs: So, Samuel died. Literally the whole country showed up for his funeral to pay their respects. He was buried in his hometown, Ramah. After that, David dipped and moved out to the Maon wilderness.

There was this super-rich guy in Maon who did business around Carmel. He had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats—dude was loaded. It was sheep-shearing season, which was a big deal. The guy's name was Nabal, which basically means 'Fool,' and his wife's name was Abigail. She was super smart and beautiful, but he was a total jerk and just plain mean—a real brute, a Calebite.

David, out in the middle of nowhere, heard Nabal was shearing his sheep. He sent ten of his guys with a message: "Go find Nabal in Carmel. Greet him for me and say, 'Hope you're doing great! Peace to you, your family, and everyone with you. I heard it's shearing time. Just so you know, when your shepherds were near us, we were cool to them. They didn't lose a single thing the whole time they were in Carmel. Ask your own guys, they'll back me up. So, what I'm asking is if you could be generous with my crew—it's a party, right? Just give whatever you feel like giving to us, your servants and your boy David.'"

David's guys went and gave Nabal the message, word for word. Nabal just blew up at them, yelling, "Who even IS this David? Who does Jesse's son think he is? The whole country is full of runaway servants these days. You think I'm gonna take the bread, wine, and meat I prepped for my own workers and just give it to some random dudes I've never even seen? I don't know where they're from!"

David's men just got out of there, went back, and told David exactly what Nabal said. David's response? "Swords on. Now." Everyone strapped on their swords, and David led 400 of his men to go handle it. The other 200 stayed behind to guard their camp.

Meanwhile, one of Nabal's own workers went straight to Abigail, Nabal's wife, and told her everything. "David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he just insulted them and screamed at them. But for real, those guys were so good to us. They never stole anything, never messed with us the whole time we were out in the fields with them. They were like a human wall, protecting us 24/7 while we were watching the sheep. You gotta do something, and fast, because some serious trouble is coming for our master and all of us. You know you can't even talk to him. He's impossible—a legit monster!"

Abigail didn't waste a second. She got 200 loaves of bread, two big skins of wine, five sheep already prepped for cooking, a ton of roasted grain, 100 raisin cakes, and 200 fig cakes, and loaded it all onto donkeys. She told her servants, "You guys go on ahead. I'll be right behind you." But she didn't say a word to her husband, Nabal.

So, as she was riding her donkey down into a ravine, she ran right into David and his men coming down from the other side. David had just been ranting, "This is just great. I wasted my time protecting everything this guy owned out in the wild so nothing got lost, and what do I get? Insults. A total slap in the face! I swear to God, if Nabal and every single guy in his crew isn't dead by morning, then let the worst happen to me!"

As soon as Abigail saw David, she jumped off her donkey, fell to her knees, and bowed with her face to the ground. She said, "Sir, please, let this all be on me! Just let me talk to you for a sec. Listen to what I have to say. Don't even think about that awful Nabal. He's literally living up to his name: Nabal, the Fool. Foolishness just pours out of him.

I wasn't there when your men arrived, I didn't even see them. But now, sir, as sure as God lives and you live, God has stopped you from taking revenge and murdering someone. May all your enemies, and anyone who wants to hurt you, end up just like Nabal! Please, take this gift that I, your servant, have brought for you, and give it to the young men who follow you.
Forgive me for being so bold! But God is working with you, my master, building you up to be a strong and solid ruler. You fight God's battles! As long as you're alive, no evil is gonna touch you.

And if anyone tries to stop you or get you out of the picture, just know this: Your life is precious to God, wrapped up safe with Him. But the lives of your enemies? He's gonna hurl them away like a rock from a sling.

When God comes through on all the good things he's promised you and makes you the leader of Israel, you don't want this on your conscience—the heavy guilt of taking revenge and killing someone for no good reason. And when God does amazing things for you, please, remember me."

And David said to her, "Wow. Praise God, the God of Israel. He's the one who sent you to meet me today! And thank God for your good sense! You are a blessing for stopping me from committing murder and taking matters into my own hands. That was a close one! As God lives, the God of Israel who kept me from hurting you, if you hadn't gotten here so fast and stopped me, I swear there wouldn't have been a single one of Nabal's guys left alive by morning."
Then David accepted her gift and told her, "Go home in peace. I've heard you, and I'll do what you asked."

When Abigail got home, Nabal was in the middle of a huge feast, like a king's party. He was in a great mood—and completely wasted. So she didn't tell him anything about what she'd done until the next morning. But in the morning, after Nabal sobered up, she told him the whole story. He had a heart attack right then and there and basically fell into a coma. About ten days later, God took him out, and he died.
When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Praise God! He stood up for me against Nabal's insults, kept me from doing something evil, and made Nabal's own evil come right back and hit him."
Then David sent a message to Abigail, asking her to be his wife. His servants went to her in Carmel and said, "David sent us to bring you to him to get married."
She got up, bowed with her face to the ground, and said, "I'm your servant, ready to do whatever you need. I'd even wash the feet of my master's servants!"
Abigail didn't wait around. She got on her donkey, and with her five maids, she followed David's messengers and became his wife.

David also married a woman named Ahinoam from Jezreel. So now they were both his wives. Meanwhile, Saul had married off David's first wife, Michal, to Palti (Paltiel) son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

title: Sneaking into the Enemy Camp: The Ultimate Glow-Up
paragraphs: Some Ziphites went to Saul at Gibeah and were like, “Yo, just so you know, David’s hiding out on Hakilah Hill, right across from Jeshimon.” Saul immediately got up and went to the Ziph wilderness with 3,000 of his best soldiers to hunt for David. He set up camp just off the road at Hakilah Hill.

David, who was still out in the country, heard that Saul was after him. He sent out spies to find out exactly where Saul was. Then David went to Saul’s camp and saw where Saul and his general, Abner son of Ner, were staying. Saul was sleeping inside the camp, surrounded by his army.
David, taking charge, talked to Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and asked, “Who’s down to go with me into Saul’s camp?”
Abishai whispered back, “I’m with you.”

So David and Abishai snuck into the camp at night. And there was Saul, passed out in the middle of the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. Abner and the soldiers were all sound asleep around him.
Abishai was like, “This is it! God has delivered your enemy to you. Let me pin him to the ground with his own spear. One shot is all I need, for real. I won’t need a second one.”
But David told Abishai, “No way, don’t hurt him! Who can attack God’s chosen king and get away with it?”

He continued, “As God is my witness, either God will take him out, or he’ll die of old age, or he’ll get killed in battle. But I’m not going to be the one to lay a hand on God’s anointed. Now, let’s just grab the spear and the water jug from his bedside and bounce.”
David took the spear and water jug from right next to Saul’s head, and they dipped. Nobody saw them. Nobody knew. Nobody even woke up! God had sent them into a deep sleep.

David then crossed over to the opposite hill and stood on top of the mountain, a safe distance away. He yelled over to the army and to Abner son of Ner, “Hey, Abner! Are you ever going to wake up and answer me?”
Abner yelled back, “Who’s that calling?”

David replied, “As God lives, aren’t you the one in charge? Why aren’t you doing your job? Why weren’t you protecting your king when someone came to kill him? That’s some bad leadership. Seriously, you and the whole bodyguard should be ashamed. And look what I’ve got—the king’s spear and water jug that were right by his head!”
By then, Saul had recognized David’s voice and said, “Is that you, my son David?”

David said, “Yeah, it’s me, my king. Why are you chasing me? What did I do? What crime have I committed? My king, listen to me. If God is the one who turned you against me, then let God be the one to sort this out. But if it’s just some people who did it, then they should be cursed. They kicked me out of my home and told me to go serve other gods. But you’re not getting rid of me that easily. You won’t separate me from God, not in life or death. This is absurd! The king of Israel is obsessed with a single flea! Hunting me down like a partridge in the hills!”
Saul confessed, “I messed up. Come back, my dear son David. I won’t hurt you anymore. You showed me respect today by sparing my life. I’ve been a fool—a total idiot.”

David answered, “Look, I have the king’s spear. Let one of your servants come and get it. God will judge us based on what’s right and who’s loyal. God put you in my hands today, but I wasn’t going to touch his anointed king. Just like I valued your life today, I hope God values my life and saves me from all my troubles.”
Saul said to David, “Bless you, my dear son David! Yes, do what you have to do! And you will succeed in everything you try!”
Then David went his way, and Saul went home.

title: Faking Out the Enemy King (for a YEAR!)
paragraphs: David was stressing, thinking to himself, "Man, sooner or later, Saul's gonna get me. The smartest move is probably to just bounce and hide out in Philistine territory. Saul will finally write me off and stop hunting me all over Israel. I'll be totally off his radar."

So David packed up and left with his six hundred guys, and they went straight to Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath. They all settled down there with the king. Each guy brought his whole family, and David brought his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel. As soon as Saul heard that David had escaped to Gath, he finally called off the manhunt.

After a bit, David said to King Achish, "Hey, if it's cool with you, could you maybe give me a spot in one of the smaller towns out in the country? It feels a little extra for me, your servant, to be living it up in the royal capital city."
So Achish gave him a town called Ziklag. (That's actually how Ziklag ended up belonging to the kings of Judah). David lived in Philistine country for a whole year and four months.

During that time, David and his guys would go out and raid the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites—these were the original inhabitants of the land stretching toward Shur as you go to Egypt. But when David raided a place, He left no one alive, not a single man or woman. He just took all their stuff: sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, clothes—everything. Then he'd go back to Achish.
Achish would always ask, "So, who'd you raid today?"

And David would lie, saying something like, "Oh, the Negev of Judah," or "The Negev of Jerahmeel," or "The Negev of the Kenites." He never left anyone alive to tell the real story, in case they showed up in Gath and exposed what he was actually doing. This was his whole strategy the entire time he lived with the Philistines.
Achish came to trust David completely. He thought, "This guy has made his own people hate him so much, he's never going to leave my side. He's stuck with me for good."

title: Saul's Ghost-Summoning Stunt Goes Horribly Wrong
paragraphs: So, around this time, the Philistines were getting their army together to go to war with Israel. Achish, the Philistine king, tells David, "Yo, just so you know, you and your guys are rolling with my army."
And David was like, "Bet. Now you'll get to see what I'm really made of."
"Awesome!" said Achish. "I'm making you my personal bodyguard—for life!"

Okay, quick backstory: Samuel was dead by now. All of Israel had a huge funeral for him and buried him in his hometown, Ramah. And way before this, Saul had kicked out all the psychics and people who claimed to talk to the dead.

The Philistines got their troops together and camped at Shunem. Saul gathered all of Israel and camped at Gilboa. But when Saul saw the massive Philistine army, he was shaking in his boots, scared to death.
Saul prayed to God, but God left him on read—no answer, not in a dream, not through a sign, not from a prophet.
So Saul told his officials, "Find me someone who can summon spirits. I need to go ask them for advice."
His servants were like, "Well, there's a witch at Endor."

Saul went full-on disguise mode, changing his clothes and everything. He took two guys with him and went to the woman's house at night. He said, "I need you to do a séance for me. Call up the spirit of the person I name."
The woman was like, "Hold up. You know what Saul did, right? How he got rid of all the mediums in the country. Are you trying to set me up and get me killed?"
Saul swore a super serious oath, "As God is my witness, you won't get in any trouble for this."
The woman finally asked, "Alright, so who do you want me to bring up?"
"Samuel. Bring up Samuel for me."
When the woman saw Samuel's spirit, she screamed at the top of her lungs and yelled at Saul, "Why did you lie to me?! You're King Saul!"
The king told her, "It's cool, you have nothing to be scared of... but what do you see?"
"I see a spirit coming up from the ground."
"And what's he look like?" Saul asked.
"An old man, coming up, and he's wearing a priest's robe."
Saul knew it was Samuel. He immediately dropped to the ground, face down, and worshiped.
Samuel said to Saul, "Why did you bother me by calling me up?"

"Because I'm in huge trouble," Saul said. "The Philistines are about to attack, and God has ghosted me—He won't answer me anymore, not by prophet or by dream. So I'm calling you to tell me what I should do."

"Why are you asking me?" Samuel shot back. "God has literally left you and is on your neighbor's side now. God did exactly what He told you through me—He's ripping the kingdom out of your hands and giving it to your neighbor. This is all happening because you didn't obey God and refused to carry out His fierce anger on the Amalekites. That's why God is doing this to you today. And it gets worse. God is going to hand over Israel, and you with it, to the Philistines. Tomorrow, you and your sons will be with me. And yeah, God is totally giving Israel's army to the Philistines."

Saul just collapsed on the ground, like a tree getting chopped down, completely terrified by what Samuel said. He had zero strength left—he hadn't eaten anything all day and all night. The woman saw he was in deep shock and said to him, "Look, I did what you asked. I risked my life for you and followed your orders exactly. Now it's your turn to listen to me. Let me get you some food. Eat it. It'll give you strength so you can get going."
He refused, "I'm not eating."

But his servants and the woman kept insisting, so he finally gave in. He got up from the floor and sat on the bed. The woman quickly went to work. She had a calf that was well-fed, and she butchered it. Then she took some flour, kneaded it, and baked some flatbread. She served it all to Saul and his servants. After they had a pretty decent meal, they got up and left that same night.

title: Kicked Out Before the Battle Even Starts?!
paragraphs: So the Philistines gathered all their troops at Aphek, while Israel was camped by the spring in Jezreel. The Philistine leaders were marching on with their units, and David and his guys were at the very back with King Achish.
The Philistine commanders were like, 'Yo, what are these Hebrews even doing here?'

Achish shot back, 'Come on, you guys know David, right? He used to work for King Saul of Israel. He's been with me for a while now, and I've got zero complaints. He's been a solid dude since the day he bounced from Saul.'

But the Philistine officers were ticked off at Achish. 'Send this guy back to his post!' they demanded. 'He's not fighting with us. He'll probably just turn on us mid-battle to get back on his master's good side. What better way to do that than by betraying us? Isn't this the same David they sing songs about?'
'Saul kills by the thousand, David by the ten thousand!'

So Achish had to call David over. 'Look, man,' he said, 'as God is my witness, you've been a loyal friend. You've been awesome to work with, and I have nothing but good things to say about you. But the other leaders just aren't having it. It's probably best if you just head out peacefully. It's not worth making them angry.'
David was like, 'But what did I do? Have you had a single problem with me since I joined you? Why can't I fight my master the king's enemies?'

'I know, I know,' Achish said. 'You're a good guy, like an angel from God in my book. But the Philistine officers were super clear: 'He's not going into battle with us.' So, just get an early start tomorrow with your men. As soon as it's light enough, just go.'
So David and his men got up early and were on their way back to Philistine territory by sunrise. The Philistines continued on to Jezreel.

title: David's Epic Comeback: The Ultimate Rescue Mission
paragraphs: So, three days later, David and his crew finally roll back into Ziklag, and it's a complete disaster. The Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag, totally trashing the town and burning it to the ground. They captured all the women, young and old. They didn't kill anyone, but basically herded them off like cattle. By the time David and his men got to the village, it was already a smoldering wreck, and their wives, sons, and daughters were all gone.

David and his guys just broke down, wailing and crying until they had nothing left. David’s two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, Nabal's widow from Carmel, were also taken. And then, things got even worse for David. His own men, bitter and heartbroken over losing their families, started talking about stoning him. His own men were practically in mutiny.
But David found his strength by trusting in his God. He told Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, 'Bring me the Ephod so I can ask God what to do.' Abiathar brought it to him.
Then David prayed to God, 'Should I go after these raiders? Can I catch them?'
The answer came back: 'Go after them! You'll definitely catch them! And you'll rescue everyone!'

So David took off with his six hundred men. They got to the Brook Besor, but some of them were too wiped to go on. David and four hundred men kept pushing forward, but two hundred of them were just too exhausted to cross the brook and had to stay behind.

Some of the guys who continued on found an Egyptian dude in a field and brought him to David. They gave him some bread and water, and he ate. They also gave him a piece of a fig cake and a couple of raisin muffins. He started to come back to life. Turns out, he hadn't eaten or drunk anything for three whole days and nights!
David asked him, 'Who's your boss? Where are you from?'

'I'm an Egyptian, a slave to an Amalekite,' he said. 'My master just left me for dead when I got sick three days ago. We had just raided the Negev of the Kerethites, Judah, and Caleb. And yeah, we're the ones who burned Ziklag.'
David asked him, 'Can you lead us to this raiding party?'
'Swear to me by God,' the guy said, 'that you won't kill me or hand me back to my old master, and I'll take you right to them.'
He led David straight to them. The Amalekites were scattered everywhere, partying it up, eating and drinking, and enjoying all the stuff they had plundered from Philistia and Judah.

David and his men attacked. They fought from sunrise until the evening of the next day. No one got away except for four hundred younger guys who escaped on camels. David rescued everything the Amalekites had taken. And he got his two wives back! Nothing and no one was missing—not the young, not the old, not a single son or daughter, and none of the loot. David recovered it all. He gathered all the sheep and cattle, and everyone was shouting, 'This is all David's loot!'

Then David went back to the two hundred men who had been too tired to continue and had stayed at the Brook Besor. They came out to welcome David and his crew. As he got closer, he shouted, 'We did it!'

But some of the selfish, rotten guys who had marched with David started complaining: 'They didn't help with the rescue, so they shouldn't get any of the plunder we recovered. They can take their wives and kids, but that's it. Tell them to take their families and leave!'

'No way, my brothers! We're a team, we don't do that,' David said, shutting down the argument. 'You can't act like this with what God has given us! God protected us. He handed over the raiders who attacked us. Who would even listen to such nonsense? The one who stays behind with the gear gets the same share as the one who goes out to fight—equal shares for everyone. Share and share alike!' From that day on, David made that a rule in Israel—and it's still the rule today.

When he got back to Ziklag, David sent parts of the plunder to the elders of Judah, his neighbors, with a note that said, 'Here’s a gift for you from the stuff we took from God’s enemies!' He sent gifts to the elders in Bethel, Ramoth Negev, Jattir, Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa, Racal, the Jerahmeelite cities, the Kenite cities, Hormah, Bor Ashan, Athach, and Hebron, and a bunch of other places where he and his men had been.

title: The King's Tragic Last Stand
paragraphs: The Philistines declared war on Israel, and the Israelite soldiers were in a full-blown retreat, falling left and right, wounded on Mount Gilboa. The Philistines zeroed in on Saul and his sons, and they ended up killing Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malki-Shua—Saul's boys.

The fighting got super intense right around Saul. The archers found their mark and he was seriously wounded. Saul told his weapon guy, “Yo, pull out your sword and just end me. I can't let these pagans come and make a whole spectacle out of killing me.”

But his weapon guy was too freaked out and wouldn't do it. So Saul just took his own sword and fell on it. When the weapon guy saw that Saul was dead, he did the exact same thing and died with him. So Saul, his three sons, and his right-hand man—they all died together that day.

When the Israelites living in the nearby valley and across the Jordan River saw that their army was bailing and that Saul and his sons were dead, they straight up abandoned their cities and ran. The Philistines just moved in and took over their homes.

The next day, when the Philistines were looting the dead, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa. They cut off Saul's head and stripped his armor. Then they paraded the news all over Philistine territory, showing it off in their idol shrines and to all the people. They put his armor on display in the temple of their goddess Ashtoreth and nailed his body to the wall at Beth Shan.

The people of Jabesh Gilead heard what the Philistines did to Saul. Their most courageous men immediately jumped into action. They traveled all night, snatched the bodies of Saul and his three sons from the wall at Beth Shan, and brought them back to Jabesh where they performed a cremation. Then they buried their bones under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh and fasted for seven days as a sign of mourning.
